title: sycl-agent integration readiness (Backend Readiness Level)
description: Declared vs achieved depth of the SYCL/XPU backend integration. `achieved_level` is COMPUTED from the gates that resolve to a run record with exit_code 0 — it is never asserted. The claim rules in skill sycl-integration/references/backend-readiness.md bind the final report to this file.

archetype.description: A=C/C++ app with a backend seam; B=C++ library+CMake+own tests; C=framework custom-op extension; D=Python array/JIT library; E=runtime/JIT-codegen system; F=graph/parser-driven engine.

target_level.description: DECLARED at scaffold. Lower it early and loudly with a reason; never lower it at report time.

achieved_level.description: COMPUTED: the highest level whose gate (and every gate below it) is `pass` with resolvable evidence.

entrypoint.description: The project's real entrypoint command exercised by the L3 gate.

backend_switch.description: How the SYCL/XPU backend is selected (build flag, CMake option, env var) and where that switch lives.

gates.description: One entry per level. Only `pass` counts toward achieved_level (L2 also accepts `partial` when `exceptions` is non-empty), and only if `evidence` resolves to a record with exit_code 0.

exceptions.description: L2 only: enumerated test failures accepted for a `partial`, one reason each. An empty list with status `partial` is invalid.

reference.description: L3: what the workload output was compared against.

tolerance.description: L3: the project's own tolerance for that comparison.

waivers.description: Anything stubbed, disabled or scoped out. A silent stub is a defect; a recorded waiver is a scoped engagement.

blast_radius.description: What stops working for a user because of this waiver.

level_impact.description: Which readiness level this waiver caps, or 'none'.

residual.description: The scoped work package for everything not reached — what turns 'we did not finish' into a next step.
